name: Ui_FieldScreen_Init
summary: Constructor of the large field/menu screen object: allocates and attaches its five parts (smith menu 0x12BC, smith sub-window 0x127C, talk window 0x3984, 0x120-byte 2D drawable, 0x26C-byte panel), then initialises the part handle tags, the two 14-byte 0xFF index tables and the 24 x 0x18 timer/slot block at +0x11C.
evidence: Caller 0x001EB390 is the create/recreate wrapper: it allocates 0x6C0 bytes, calls this function and stores the result in the owner. Inside, the first three allocations are made by the already-named Ui_SmithMenu_Ctor, Ui_SmithMenu_SubWindow_Ctor and Ui_TalkWindow_Ctor, and Ui_Object_CreatePartsFromTable performs the attach; that fixes the composite-constructor role, although the screen own menu name stays generic.

name: maybe_Battle_ActionSequence_ShowActionResults
summary: One phase of the battle action-sequence state machine (states 0x175D-0x17A6): waits until every actor is idle, queues the actor name changes, plays the step sounds and the number popups of the resolved action list, and advances the turn once the pending-action counter is used up.
evidence: Correction: there is no target-picker call in the body - 0x001FE494 is Text_QueueActorNameChange (name-plate helper), so 'SelectTargets' was wrong. The body calls Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnNumberList, Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnForActorList, maybe_Battle_ActionSequence_PlayStepSounds and AdvanceTurn, i.e. it plays back the resolved results; DispatchCommand (0x3219E4) reaches it as the battle-context phase-1 branch (+0x293 == 1).

name: maybe_Battle_ActionSequence_ShowCommandResults
summary: Same playback machinery as 0x0031FDB8 for the '>' command block (state base 0x18D0): queue the actor names, play the sounds and number popups and advance the turn when the action counter is done.
evidence: Correction: the body is a near-copy of 0x0031FDB8 (same Text_QueueActorNameChange / SpawnNumberList / SpawnForActorList sequence, same AdvanceTurn tail) with the state base 0x18D0; DispatchCommand calls it from the '>' command case (unit+0x58), so it shows that command's results rather than 'running' the command.

name: maybe_Battle_ActionSequence_AdvanceAction
summary: One phase (state 0x17DC) of the battle action sequence: once the current actor is idle it dispatches the actor next queued action and clears its slots; when the per-actor counter reaches the pending-action count it calls AdvanceTurn and sets the +0xDE46 done flag.
evidence: Correction: the body advances the actor action list, not the actor - it increments self+0xDDF0 and compares it with Battle_ActionSequence_GetPendingActionCount, calling DispatchAction/ClearActionSlots in the loop and AdvanceTurn only when the count is used up. DispatchCommand (0x3219E4) reaches it for phase bytes 3/4/7.

name: Battle_ActionSequence_CheckFinish
summary: Finish check for the phase set 0x17BD/0x17C1/0x17CC: runs the same dispatch/clear/advance loop as AdvanceActor and returns 1 once the actor queue is drained, setting the +0xDE46 done flag; returns 0 while the actors are still busy.
evidence: Same body shape as 0x00320358 but with its own state base and a boolean result; DispatchCommand calls it for the phase bytes 0/5/6, i.e. exactly the phases where no further actor action is expected.

name: Battle_ActionSequence_GetPendingActionCount
summary: Returns how many action executions the current action has (func_0048EDD0 over the action id at +0x125C), tripled when the battle multi-action flag at battle-work +0x4244 is set.
evidence: Every sequence step (DispatchCommand, AdvanceActor, CheckFinish, Update 0x4F7320, Sequence_Update 0x5A407C) uses it as the loop bound compared against the +0x377C/+0xDDF0 counters, which fixes it as the per-action execution count; the x3 branch is gated on battle work +0x4244.

name: maybe_Battle_ActionSequence_NotifyUiActors
signature: void maybe_Battle_ActionSequence_NotifyUiActors(BattleActionSequence* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Marks the current actor in state 0x75 through vtable+0xE4 and then loops the UI list at battle+0x4260/+0x4264 calling 0x002789C8(object, actor) for each entry.
evidence: The only caller is DispatchCommand's command-char branch, and the loop target 0x002789C8 is still unnamed, so whether these objects are UI actors or effect/prop nodes cannot be decided; kept as maybe_.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_PushActorStateMessage
summary: Posts one popup message for the current actor: message id 0x4B when the actor state is 9, otherwise the literal id at 0x003C4AAC, handed to Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnForActorPair as an {actor, index, id} descriptor.
evidence: Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnForActorPair (0x3FC760) is now named, which confirms the popup-queue role, but both ids are unnamed literals and the function tail is a bogus call/halt_baddata, so the exact 'actor state message' meaning stays unproven.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_CreateActionPane
summary: Builds the battle action panes: creates an action-animation entry, initialises four action panes with Ui_ActionPane_Init and installs them with Container_SlotReplace into slots 0..3.
evidence: Named callees Battle_ActionAnimEntry_Create, Ui_ActionPane_Init and Container_SlotReplace confirm the pane-creation role; the decompilation is cut by an unresolved conditional (32 damaged tokens, unaff_ registers) so the surrounding state logic is missing - kept as maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_FieldActionListWindow_Init
signature: void maybe_Ui_FieldActionListWindow_Init(UiWindow* self, void* owner, u32 arg3, int arg4)
summary: Thumb twin of the field action-list builder 0x003E6634: creates the six-row 'action' list container (nut/move/dash/jump/auto rows) with Battle_ActionAnimEntry_Create and installs it with Container_SlotReplace.
evidence: Same body as 0x003E6634 but with a damaged prologue (iStack_20 computed from arg2-0x1E5FFF8E lost two argument registers); only the callee pair is trustworthy, so the entry point stays maybe_.

name: Field_ModelObj_UpdateEffect
summary: Per-object update that creates the 2D sprite of a field model object from its effect record: resolves the effect entry with Model_FindChildOfClass/Model_CountChildrenOfClass, builds the sprite through Gfx_Scene_CreateSpritesFromResource and Field_ModelObj_CreateSprite and attaches the 0x70-byte wrapper as a child.
evidence: Named callees Field_ModelObj_CreateSprite (0x4FAC78, the alternate entry of 0x4FABC0), Gfx_Scene_CreateSpritesFromResource and Model_FindChildOfClass/CountChildrenOfClass form the standard sprite-from-resource path used by Field_MultiPart_CreateSpriteFromResource too; the vtable-slot entry (0x767C70) and the 'fCol' animator side table show this is the update hook that (re)creates the sprite when the effect record changes.

name: Container_ObjectRef_Release
summary: Releases a 5-word object reference: when both the owner pointer (+4) and the element count (+8) are set it frees the buffer through owner vtable+0x14 and clears +4..+0x10.
evidence: Now seen from the caller side: Font_CacheGlyphsForText and Gfx_Scene_CreateSpritesFromResource call it immediately before overwriting their cached sub-object, and the tiny ctor 0x58D2BC builds the same 5-word struct - the release-and-clear semantics are supported.

name: maybe_Field_ActorActionSeq_UpdateAlt
summary: Second field actor action-sequence runner (states 0x1A23..0x1AA5): runs the current entry, applies the sound/camera side effects and advances or ends the sequence.
evidence: Structurally the same machine as 0x003BF564 (same 100-byte entries at +0x70C, same Sound_PlaySeById, FieldParty_UpdateStateMachine and Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnMultiActor calls) with a different state base; nothing calls it directly and it has no data reference, so which object owns it stays open.

name: Battle_TargetMarker_Update
summary: Per-frame update of the battle target markers for the current state: rebuilds the candidate list, collects the slot flags, sorts and assigns the free marker slots.
evidence: Named callees Battle_TargetMarker_BuildCandidates / CollectSlotFlags / AssignFreeSlot are now resolved, and Battle_Update (0x16E3E0) calls it, so the marker-update role is proven; only the slot ordering details remain guessed.

name: Field_Object2D_ConfirmInteraction
summary: Player-confirm branch of a field 2D object: clears the latch byte +0x29A; if the per-map byte is 1 or 4 it posts script command 0x19/0x1A via Event_OnTriggerCommand, otherwise it plays the confirm SE, stops the stored animation and sends command 0x18 through Field_Gadget_AddAndTriggerCommand.
evidence: Event_OnTriggerCommand, Sound_PlaySeById, Field_Object2D_SetConfirmMessage and Field_Gadget_AddAndTriggerCommand are all named and form the two halves of the confirm path; the function is a vtable override, so the absence of a direct caller is expected. (The earlier evidence sentence about a confirm-message setter described the neighbouring setter, not this body.)

name: maybe_Ui_RankWindow_Update
summary: State-checked entry of the rank/list window update: when the window is visible (state bits at +0x174) and flagged as state 1 it tail-calls 0x41D8F8 (the row updater) with r0=self+0x980 and the three signed cursor bytes at +0x176..+0x178; otherwise it clears a u16 at work+0x94.
evidence: Correction: the disassembly at 0x0041D888 (asm/text/text_00400048.s) is only the state test plus a tail call into 0x41D8F8 with the cursor deltas - and the pager_num_l/txt_txt strings at 0x41D734-0x41D754 lie before the function, so the old 'UpdatePager' reading came from the neighbour's data.

name: maybe_Ui_RankWindow_UpdateRows
signature: void maybe_Ui_RankWindow_UpdateRows(UiRankWindow* self, int delta, int mode, u32 arg4)
summary: Rebuilds the eight rank rows: rebinds the row rank icons with Ui_RankIcon_Bind, applies the cursor delta to the row texts and toggles the pager panes.
evidence: Only reached as the tail call from 0x41D888, which passes three signed cursor deltas; the body is the damaged second half of that Ghidra function (in_d8/unaff_r6 split), so only the eight Ui_RankIcon_Bind calls are verified - kept at 0.3.

name: maybe_Ui_EightRowTextWindow_InitPanes
signature: void maybe_Ui_EightRowTextWindow_InitPanes(UiWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 arg5)
summary: Initialises an eight-row text window: attaches the eight 'txt_l1'.. panes (digit-incremented base name) and binds each row's rank icon with Ui_RankIcon_Bind.
evidence: Ui_RankIcon_Bind (0x299B94) as the per-row callee is new and shows the rows carry rank medals, but with no caller and no pager the owning screen is still unknown - kept as maybe_.

name: maybe_Field_Object2D_UpdateCameraRelativeSprite
summary: Keeps a camera-facing sprite glued to its owner: advances along the distance curve with Math_Curve_GetPosition/GetTangent, rebuilds the billboard basis, draws the sprite variant and moves the owner's draw offset; releases the effect when the curve is exhausted.
evidence: Named callees Math_Curve_GetPosition/GetTangent, Gfx_Scene_SpriteCtx_Init and Gfx_EffectPart_SetDirection support the curve/billboard description, but no named caller exists (0x41F6D0 is itself unnamed), so the 'camera-relative' part stays inferred.

name: Field_MultiPart_CreateSpriteFromResource
summary: Creates a part's sprite from the scene resource id stored on the actor record and caches it at scene-context +0x120, then attaches the 0x70-byte wrapper holding the part frame data.
evidence: Callees Gfx_Scene_CreateSpritesFromResource, Field_ModelObj_CreateSprite and Model_FindChildOfClass are named now and form the standard sprite-from-resource path; its twin 0x44E718 uses the other cache slot (+0x118).

name: Field_MultiPart_CreateSpriteFromResourceB
summary: Second sprite-from-resource path of the multi-part object: same as 0x44E4D0 but caches the created sprite in the other scene slot (+0x118).
evidence: Byte-for-byte twin of 0x44E4D0 apart from the cache offset (0x118 vs 0x120) and the same named callees, so it is the B variant of the same resource-to-sprite step.

name: Text_CalcRowHeightEx
signature: int Text_CalcRowHeightEx(int arg1, int arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, int arg5, int arg6)
summary: Computes the height of a text row including the 1.0/1.2 line scaling and the row padding, storing the result in the row at +0x52.
evidence: Now known to be called from Text_ApplyRowStyle (0x488638) next to Text_CalcRowBox/Text_MeasureElement, i.e. the row-style pass; the 1.0/1.2 literals and the +0x52 store match the height computation.

name: Text_CalcRowGeometry
signature: void Text_CalcRowGeometry(int arg1, u32* arg2, int arg3)
summary: Lays out one text row: fills the row layout context (Text_Row_Init/Text_Row_TryLayout, Text_CalcGlyphAdvance) and copies the measured rectangle into the row; message id 0x33 is special-cased.
evidence: Named callees Text_Row_TryLayout, Text_CalcGlyphAdvance and the Battle_Message_BuildConditionRow/BuildRowForMonsterEx pair appear inside the function, i.e. the row-geometry step of the message layout; it is called from 0x424CA8, which builds a row entry.

name: Text_CalcRowSpacing
signature: u32 Text_CalcRowSpacing(int arg1, int arg2, u32 arg3, int* arg4)
summary: Computes the vertical spacing around a row: 100.0 or 62.5 pixels depending on the row kind (0x22), scaled by 0.01, and marks the layout dirty.
evidence: Called from Text_ApplyRowStyle (0x488638) together with Text_CalcRowBox/Text_IsRowVisible/Text_MarkLayoutDirty, which fixes it as part of the row-style measurement; the 100.0/62.5/0.01 literals match.

name: maybe_Text_CalcRowBaseline
signature: int maybe_Text_CalcRowBaseline(int self, int arg2, u32 arg3)
summary: Computes the baseline of a text row: anchors to the actor box when the run has an actor, otherwise uses the row table at +0xC4..+0xCA and the type-height lookup.
evidence: Text_IsRowVisible and Game_GetDataManager are the only named callees and the caller (0x4F358C) is itself still maybe_, so the 'baseline' reading rests on the field layout and the type compares alone.

name: maybe_Text_CalcRowBaselineEx
signature: int maybe_Text_CalcRowBaselineEx(int self, int arg2, u32 arg3)
summary: Alternate baseline calculation for the row types 0x94/0x96/0x97 using the type-height table and the actor box; no direct caller.
evidence: Same type compares and f_18/f_1C min/max logic as 0x48A63C but nothing calls it (inlined twin), so the name comes only from the shared structure.

name: maybe_Text_BuildRowFromTemplate
signature: int maybe_Text_BuildRowFromTemplate(u32 arg1, int arg2, u32 arg3, float arg4, u32 arg5, int arg6, int arg7)
summary: Builds a battle message row from the fixed template table: checks the flag word (+0x296), the row kind and the monster action category, then applies the template layout.
evidence: Text_IsRowVisible plus the Battle_Message_* row builders and the +0x296 flag test match the row-builder shape, but there is no caller and the template table is unnamed, so it stays maybe_.

name: Text_Window_SetCharRevealTiming
signature: void Text_Window_SetCharRevealTiming(TextWindow* self, GlyphOwner* run, u32 charCode)
summary: Sets the typewriter timing for one text run: base delay from the glyph record plus a random jitter in [0, glyph->f_2E], stored in the short at +0x125C together with the custom-timing byte at +0x125E.
evidence: These are exactly the two fields the typewriter tick 0x4F3334 reads (count + flag), and the body now shows Game_GetDataManager(row)->f_28/f_2E feeding the battle RNG (ctx+0x4218) for the jitter - the reveal-timing role holds.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_ShowMemberRefText
summary: Shows the text reference attached to a member row: checks Text_IsRowVisible and posts the referenced row through Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnFromTable; installed as slot 0x28 of the six identical message-window vtables.
evidence: Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnFromTable and Text_IsRowVisible are named, but the class owning the vtable slot is not identified, so 'MemberRefText' is still a guess.

name: maybe_Text_CalcRowValueFromActor
signature: int maybe_Text_CalcRowValueFromActor(int arg1, int arg2, int arg3, int arg4)
summary: Computes the numeric value shown in a row from the actor fields: picks f_18/f_1C or their min/max according to the row record byte +0x2A; ids 0x5F/0x30 are special-cased.
evidence: Same caller set as the text row builders (0x4F4314, 0x4F358C) and only Text_IsRowVisible as a named callee; the 'row value' meaning stays inferred from the record-byte switch.

name: maybe_Ui_Entry_ClearRecord
summary: Zero-fills a UI entry record before the caller fills it in: 0x59 bytes through 0x001113EC plus a zero byte at +0x59. The same record type is used for message-page commands, battle UI-flow entries, command-list rows and member masks.
evidence: Disassembly 0x004A4BB4: r0=record, r1=0x59, bl 0x001113EC (MemZero) then strb r4=0 at [record+0x59]. Named callers are Ui_MessagePage_ExecuteCommand, Battle_UiFlow_EvaluateCondition, Battle_CommandListWindow_BuildEntries and maybe_Menu_BuildMemberMask, so the entry is generic UI bookkeeping, not a battle Condition; the old word was too narrow and is replaced.

name: Ui_ItemListWindow_BuildItemRow
signature: void Ui_ItemListWindow_BuildItemRow(UiItemListWindow* self, const ItemRecord* item, unsigned int arg3, void* item_table)
summary: Builds one item row of a shop/equipment list: item name, quantity, the comparison arrow chosen by comparing the equipped id (f_388) with the candidate id (f_38A), and the price, then hides the unused list rows.
evidence: Named callees Ui_TextLayer_SetText, Text_SetFormatArgsFromPlayerData, Ui_ListWindow_HideUnusedRows and the item resolver func_0035EB98 fix the row builder; the body writes the panes for one item and the 0xB loop is over columns, so the previous plural Rows was misleading.

name: Ui_ItemListWindow_BuildRowsFromRecord
signature: void Ui_ItemListWindow_BuildRowsFromRecord(UiItemListWindow* self, const void* record, unsigned int arg3, void* item_table)
summary: Simplified four-row item list builder: string, name, two empty columns and one value from the same item tables, without the equipped-comparison arrow.
evidence: Same table accesses and Ui_ListWindow_HideUnusedRows tail as 0x5A2B30 but with a four-row limit and no g_005A304C arrow lookup, which now distinguishes the record variant from the item variant.

name: maybe_Ui_ListWindow_FillStatRows
signature: void maybe_Ui_ListWindow_FillStatRows(UiListWidget* self, const void* stats, int arg3, void* callback)
summary: Generic stat-list filler: walks the eleven-entry getter table g_004FB394 (icon byte, getter, extra flag), formats each value into its pane row and blanks the remaining columns.
evidence: Ui_ListWindow_HideUnusedRows is the only named callee and the function is reached only through the 0x77D9EC filler dispatch table, so which screen's stats these are is still open.

name: maybe_Ui_ListWindow_FillExtraRows
signature: void maybe_Ui_ListWindow_FillExtraRows(UiListWidget* self, const void* source, unsigned int arg3, void* callback)
summary: Second list filler: writes six panes per row (text id 0xAA plus a number) from its own getter table g_005AEDDC and appends a generic icon in column 4.
evidence: Same skeleton as 0x4FB1CC with a different table and dispatch entry (0x77F4A8); no named caller and no strings, so the owning list stays unknown.

name: Sq_Vm_InitThread
signature: u32 Sq_Vm_InitThread(SqVM* thread, SqVM* parent, u32 stackSize)
summary: Initialises a newly allocated Squirrel VM thread: resizes its value stack and call stack, resets the stack/call pointers, creates a fresh root hash table when there is no parent (otherwise shares the parent tables at +0x38/+0x48/+0x50) and registers the system globals.
evidence: Correction: Script_Vm_Create (0x6BC454) and Script_Vm_PushStackFrame (0x6BC2AC) call this immediately after allocating the 0xA8-byte thread object, and the body is Sq_Stack_Resize + Sq_Vm_ResizeCallStack + root-table setup + Script_RegisterSystemGlobals - the sq_newthread initialisation, not a call-stack snapshot. The old name described the resize calls as if they captured frames.

name: maybe_BattleScene_UpdateUnitModel
signature: int maybe_BattleScene_UpdateUnitModel(BattleScene* self, BattleUnit* unit, int arg3)
summary: Per-state model refresh of one battle unit: walks the four unit lists, skips units whose model is already attached, merges the animation tracks for the unit variant and builds/positions its member model.
evidence: The named callees BattleScene_GetUnitModelVariant, BattleScene_BuildMemberModel, BattleScene_PositionUnitModelWithAnim and Anim_TimeTrack_MergeDuplicates describe the whole rebuild, but there is no caller and the B suffix distinguished nothing - the exact phase (attach vs. per-frame update) is not proven.

name: maybe_BattleScene_UpdateUnitSlots
summary: Refreshes the battle unit slots: walks the four unit lists, assigns free model slots by unit variant, unlinks released actors and repositions each unit model for the current state.
evidence: Named callees BattleScene_GetUnitModelVariant, BattleScene_PositionUnitModelWithAnim and Container_List_CountVisible plus the slot table at g_0060A45C show the slot bookkeeping, but the caller BattleScene_UpdateState attribution is unverified and the old UnitList0 label named an index that the body does not use.

name: Ui_ListCursor_GetSelectedMemberIdB
summary: Same body as 0x0063A9E0: returns the party member id at the current cursor, or 0x1F when the cursor is past the active member count.
evidence: Disassembly 0x0063B5A0..0x0063B5E0 is byte-identical to 0x0063A9E0 (Party_GetActiveMemberCount bound, Party_GetMemberIdAtIndex tail call), so the old GetSlotFlags name was wrong - the body never reads a flags byte. The B suffix marks the duplicate entry point.

name: Ui_ListCursor_IsAtPartyEndRow
summary: True when the list cursor index equals the active party-member count, i.e. the cursor sits on the first row after the party member rows.
evidence: Both operands are named accessors (func_0063A794 = cursor, Party_GetActiveMemberCount = row count) and the disassembly is a plain cmp/return; the predicate is mechanically certain. It is the same predicate as 0x0063AA24, which is the B copy.

name: Ui_ListCursor_IsAtPartyEndRowPlus1
summary: True when the list cursor index is exactly active-member-count + 1, i.e. the second row after the party member rows.
evidence: Disassembly 0x0063B60C: add r0,r0,#1 after Party_GetActiveMemberCount, then cmp with the cursor accessor. The named callers (Ui_EquipmentWindow_Confirm/FindItemIndex/Update) use it to choose the pane, but the mechanical meaning is just count+1.

name: Ui_ListCursor_IsPastPartyEndRows
summary: True when the list cursor index is two or more past the active party-member count (cursor >= count + 2).
evidence: Disassembly 0x0063B638 adds 2 to Party_GetActiveMemberCount and returns the signed >= comparison against the cursor accessor; same pane-selection role as 0x0063B5E4/0x63B60C.

name: Ui_ListCursor_GetSelectedMemberId
summary: Returns the party member id under the list cursor (Party_GetMemberIdAtIndex on the +0x410 party sub-object) when the cursor is inside the active member rows, otherwise the sentinel id 0x1F.
evidence: Both callees are named now: Party_GetActiveMemberCount is the bound and Party_GetMemberIdAtIndex returns entity+0xC8, i.e. a member id, not a party count slot. Callers are the item/shop list cursor handlers.

name: Ui_ListCursor_IsPastPartyRows
summary: True when the cursor index is at or past the active party-member count (count <= cursor); Ui_TsuyosaWindow_OnInput uses it to stop scrolling onto the trailing extra rows.
evidence: Called from Ui_TsuyosaWindow_OnInput (0x2A0BE0); the body compares Party_GetActiveMemberCount with the cursor accessor func_0063A794, so the predicate is mechanically a count <= cursor test (the previous fits-inside-the-page wording mis-read the cursor as a page bound).

name: maybe_Ui_BagList_SetLabel
signature: void maybe_Ui_BagList_SetLabel(UiBagList* self, int row, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Shows the selected bag row, or - when the row is out of range - the bag-name label id 0xD (tool bag) or 0xE (equipment bag) chosen by the object's +0x5 flag.
evidence: Callees Party_GetActiveMemberCount/Ui_GetCore and the emission through 0x633560 are named, but the two text ids are untranslated placeholders and no caller identifies the window.

name: Ui_ListCursor_IsAtOrPastPartyEndRow
summary: True when the cursor index is at or past the active party-member count (count <= cursor), i.e. the cursor has left the real member rows.
evidence: Correction: iVar1 is the cursor index (func_0063A794), not a last row of the page; the body returns Party_GetActiveMemberCount <= cursor. The old visible wording inverted the meaning.

name: Ui_ListCursor_IsAtPartyEndRowB
summary: Same predicate as 0x0063B5E4: true when the cursor index equals the active party-member count (first row after the members).
evidence: The body is Party_GetActiveMemberCount == cursor accessor; it is a template copy of 0x0063B5E4 used by the shop list handlers. The old IsAtLastRow label wrongly treated the member count as a page bound.

name: Ui_ListCursor_IsOnePastPartyEndRow
summary: True when the cursor index equals active-member-count + 1 (the second row after the party members).
evidence: The body is the same count+1 comparison as 0x0063B60C (Party_GetActiveMemberCount + 1 == cursor); the shop list handlers use both copies. Corrected wording: it is one past the party end row, not past the last row of an unknown page.

name: maybe_Ui_ListCursor_GetFirstFreeRow
summary: Returns the first row index after the page's data (count + 1, or count + 2 when the mode byte at +4 is set), used to place the trailing blank/summary row.
evidence: No caller at all, and this copy lost arg1 of Party_GetActiveMemberCount, so the row arithmetic can only be read from the constants.

name: maybe_Party_GetRowCountPlusThree
summary: Returns the active party-member count + 3, the row index of a fixed extra row (summary row) appended by the bag/equipment list builders.
evidence: The whole body is Party_GetActiveMemberCount() + 3; there is no caller and no list object, so which extra row the +3 addresses cannot be proven. Renamed from GetSummaryRowIndex to state only what the code does.

name: maybe_Party_GetRowCountPlusOne
summary: Returns the active party member count + 1, i.e. the index of the first row after the party rows.
evidence: Correction: the body is Party_GetActiveMemberCount() + 1, so the old name GetRowCountPlusTwo contradicted the code; there is still no caller, so which list appends that row stays open.

name: maybe_Ui_List_GetRowCount
summary: Returns the number of rows a party list needs: the active member count plus one when the object extra-row flag at +4 is set.
evidence: Only Party_GetActiveMemberCount is named and there is no caller; the +4 flag also selects count+2 in 0x0063AB0C. Renamed from GetDisplayedRowCount because the function does not read any display/page bound.

name: maybe_Ui_List_IsCursorAtPartyEndRow
summary: Same predicate as 0x0063B5E4 applied to a list sub-object: true when its cursor index equals the active party-member count.
evidence: The two named accessors are the same ones used by 0x0063B5E4/0x0063AA24 (cursor accessor and Party_GetActiveMemberCount on list+0x410); the caller maybe_Ui_EquipmentList_Scroll (0x199B60) is still a maybe_, so the class stays unnamed, but the comparison is a party-end-row test.

name: Anim_Curve_Dispatch
summary: Normalises the curve time ratio (Math_ComputeNormalizedRatio) and tail-calls the per-type/per-mode evaluator from the 0x20-byte-stride table at 0x007AE7C8, index type*0x20 + mode*4.
evidence: Every Anim_CurveEval_F*M* and Anim_CurveSample_F*M* readable header (for example Anim_CurveSample_F3M4_006ed904.c) names 0x0065B890 as the dispatcher that selects it from the curve two type bytes, and the named callers are Anim_Track_EvaluateVec3/Vec4/Transform. The old Math_EvaluateInterpolator name put an animation-curve dispatcher in the wrong subsystem.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_CompositeDtor
summary: Tears down the composite message window: destroys the message-page array with Ui_MessagePage_Dtor, releases the embedded layout refs (Ui_LayoutRef_Release), unlinks the inline node lists and runs the shared finaliser.
evidence: Named callees Ui_MessagePage_Dtor/Ui_LayoutRef_Release/Ui_Object_DtorBase and the caller 0x3D8A40 (deleting dtor) match, but the exact class (message-window composite vs. a wider Ui_Node class) is not fixed.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_ConstructPartsB
summary: Base-part constructor of a large composite-window family: installs the vtable and then builds a fixed chain of embedded sub-widgets with Ui_Object_DtorBase/Ui_MessagePage_Dtor table copies.
evidence: Reached only through descriptor table 0x0072C788 and its only caller is the deleting dtor 0x264CE0; with no literals or named class, the 'Window' family member is a guess.

name: maybe_Ui_CompositeWindow_InitPartsH
summary: Compact composite constructor: installs the vtable, builds the trailing pane chain (two inline list inits and one 0x38-byte helper object) and ends with 0x36B514 + 0x1D8C2C + 0x10F6CC.
evidence: No caller and no literal; only the shared dtor/table idiom identifies it as another member of the composite-window family, so the family name is all that is known.

name: maybe_Ui_Composite_DtorDelete
signature: void maybe_Ui_Composite_DtorDelete(unsigned int* self, unsigned int vtable)
summary: Deleting destructor of a composite UI object: reinitialises both intrusive child lists, destroys the child array, runs Ui_Object_DtorBase and frees the object.
evidence: Ui_Object_DtorBase (0x1A6768) and the list-sentinel writes are the only named anchors; no caller, so the owning class stays unknown.

name: maybe_Ui_Panel_Delete
summary: Out-of-line release+delete of a panel: stores the passed vtable, unlinks the child list at +0x88, destroys the child with Ui_Object_DtorBase and frees the panel.
evidence: Pack_ReleaseHandle appears in the body beside Ui_Object_DtorBase, so the object also owns a pack handle; no caller identifies the class, so 'panel' is generic.

name: maybe_Ui_LargeWindow_DeleteMembers
summary: Destructor of a very large composite window: repairs six intrusive lists, destroys two embedded UI objects with Ui_Object_DtorBase and releases the layout reference at +0x138.
evidence: Only Ui_Object_DtorBase is named; the function is vtable-only, so 'large window' is inferred from the size of the object it walks.

name: maybe_Ui_ComplexWindow_DtorMember
summary: Twenty-byte thunk: Ui_Object_DtorBase followed by operator delete - a member deleting-destructor of some UI class.
evidence: Same two-call shape as 0x323AC8/0x324304; the 'complex window' owner comes only from the neighbouring 0x29CF34 vtable, so the class is unproven.

name: maybe_Ui_ListWidget_Ctor
summary: Allocates and constructs a list widget: vtable 0x007612F0, two self-referential intrusive list heads at +0x13C/+0x14C, embedded node vtable 0x00759388 and eight cleared words.
evidence: Its only caller is Battle_TextWindow_Ctor (0x213578), which fits a list widget owned by a text window, but the class name is still generic.

name: maybe_Battle_Popup_DtorBase
summary: Sixteen-byte destructor thunk: Ui_Object_DtorBase followed by operator delete, with no vtable store.
evidence: Twin of 0x324304 and 0x325A34; vtable-only and the class is unnamed, so the 'battle popup' attribution rests on its position in the battle UI block.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleWindow_DtorBase
summary: Sixteen-byte destructor thunk: Ui_Object_DtorBase followed by operator delete, with no vtable store; twin of 0x323AC8.
evidence: Same body as 0x323AC8/0x325A34 and no caller, so neither the class nor the 'battle window' part is proven.

name: maybe_Ui_Object_DeleteViaVtable
summary: Deleting-destructor thunk for a Ui_Object: runs Ui_Object_DtorBase and then dispatches the real delete through the vtable slot at object-8 (multiple-inheritance delete).
evidence: Ui_Object_DtorBase is the only named callee and the virtual call at (obj-8)+4 is the standard MI-delete idiom; no caller confirms the class.

name: maybe_Field_LampGimmick_DtorBase
summary: Deleting destructor of the lamp-gimmick base object: chains to Ui_Object_DtorBase and frees the allocation; it sits in the vtable slot right after the constructor 0x4FA204.
evidence: Only Ui_Object_DtorBase is named; the 'lamp gimmick' owner comes from the neighbouring 0x77CF14 vtable entry (0x4FA204), which is itself unnamed.

name: maybe_Ui_TextLayout_AppendElementRunA
signature: int maybe_Ui_TextLayout_AppendElementRunA(UiTextLayout* self, u32 index, u32 category, u32 arg4, int allowAll)
summary: Appends the text runs of one element of the layout's first content list: resolves the id, checks the record flag and the filter bit, then creates one run per glyph/child and appends the candidate.
evidence: Named callees Ui_TextLayout_AppendCandidateFromWidget, Text_BuildRowForMember, Battle_Message_ApplyRowLayout and Ui_TextLayout_CheckFilterBit place it in the text-layout builder, but the body is a damaged decompilation (bad instruction data, unaff_r8) so the entry/summary wording cannot be narrowed further.

name: maybe_Ui_Layout_LoadNamedObjects
summary: Instantiates the objects named in a UI layout: creates the primary and secondary objects through the object factory, replaces the previous handles and wires them into the layout's child slots.
evidence: Callee names now include Mem_AllocAligned_2 and the object factory, but its callers are Ui_SceneFlow_OpenScene6 (0x1A0130) and Field2D_Scene_InitSpawnPoints, which is odd for a pure UI loader, so the scope is still uncertain.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_ShowNamePlate
signature: void maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_ShowNamePlate(UiMessageWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Creates and shows the 0x260-byte plate window attached at +0x18 (speaker name / small extra window) and marks the window as two-plate mode.
evidence: Mem_AllocAligned_2/Ui_Object_CreatePartsFromTable/Ui_GetCore are named but there is no caller (vtable slot), so the 'name plate' purpose rests on the +0x18 attach and the f_40=2 store.

name: maybe_Field_CreateSmallEffect
summary: Creates a small (0x28-byte) field object and submits it into a container slot; the Thumb entry lost r4/r6, so only the allocation/submit calls are trustworthy.
evidence: Mem_AllocAligned_2 and Container_SlotReplace are named, but the body is a damaged thumb decompilation (unaff_r4/r6) and nothing identifies the object kind.

name: maybe_Model_NodeCtor_782140
summary: Allocation-free constructor wrapper for a small model node: obtains storage from 0x00579974 and installs vtable 0x00782140 with a cleared tail word.
evidence: Only Mem_AllocAligned_2 and the 0x579974 storage helper are named; no caller, and vtable 0x00782140 has no named method, so the node kind is unknown.

name: maybe_Gfx_NodeCtor_7826E8
summary: Constructor wrapper for a graphics node: storage from 0x00579974, vtable 0x007826E8 and eleven zero stores.
evidence: Structurally identical to 0x56D6D4/0x5AB860 with a different vtable; no caller or named method, so 'Gfx node' is a guess.

name: maybe_Model_NodeCtor_783470
summary: Constructor wrapper for a model node: storage from 0x00579974, vtable 0x00783470 and five trailing words cleared.
evidence: Same three-call shape as 0x56D6D4/0x576E9C; nothing in the body names the class.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_HandleCancel
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_HandleCancel(BattleWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, int arg4)
summary: Battle command-window cancel branch: stops the current command animation and, if an action was pending (f_130 & 0x102), reverses it and returns the window to the previous step.
evidence: The file is a recovered entry point with a damaged body (halt_baddata), and the named neighbours (Ui_BattleEnemyListWindow_IsRowSelectable, Ui_BattlePopup_Show) fit both a cancel and a confirm path.

name: Ui_PartyPanel_CheckMembersReady
summary: Counts the battle party members whose actor object is available and idle and, if the counts allow it, continues the panel with the confirm message args and state 8; otherwise it refreshes the window.
evidence: Callees Menu_CountPartyActors, Sound_PlaySeById and Ui_BattlePopup_Show are named, and the walk over the +0x4254 actor table with vtable+0xF0 validity checks matches the 'members ready' question.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_HandleConfirm
summary: Confirm branch of the battle command window: resolves the highlighted command, shows its pop-up preview and moves the window to the target-selection step.
evidence: Callees Ui_BattlePopup_Show/Sound_PlaySeById are named but the control flow is damaged ('bad instruction data'), so the confirm semantics cannot be separated from the neighbouring handler.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_HandleCommandPage
summary: Pages the battle command list forward/backward and updates the highlight when no confirm event is pending.
evidence: Only Menu_ClearActorUiFlag, Ui_BattlePopup_Show and Sound_PlaySeById are named and there is no caller; the paging reading comes from the +0x102/+4 state bits alone.

name: Ui_PartyPanel_ConfirmMemberSlots
summary: Confirm handler of the party-panel window: validates the current member slot selection with Ui_PartyPanel_HasRequiredMembers, plays the confirm sound, refreshes the four status panels and advances the controller state.
evidence: Named callees Ui_PartyPanel_HasRequiredMembers, Ui_PartyPanel_SelectMemberRow and Ui_BattleTargetWindow_RefreshAllTargets pin the validation-and-refresh step; it is reached only from the window's own state controller, not by a direct call.

name: Ui_PartyPanel_SwapMembers
summary: Performs the party-member swap chosen in the panel: maps the two stored member ids to actor slots in the +0x24A98 id table, calls the swap helper 0x4025BC and Menu_SelectPartyPair, then sets the message args and advances to state 8.
evidence: Named callees Sound_PlaySeById/Ui_BattlePopup_Show plus the 0x1F-entry walk over GameWork+0x24A98 (party/bag storage) and the two stored ids at self[0x7D]/self[0x7E] make the swap role concrete.

name: Ui_BattleWindow_ShowPopupMessage
summary: Shows one of the fixed battle pop-up texts (ids 0x8B4..0x8B7) through Ui_BattlePopup_Show, choosing the variant from a global config byte, then releases the auxiliary message window.
evidence: Callees Ui_BattlePopup_Show, Ui_MessageWindow_ProcessCommands and Ui_MessageWindow_ReleaseLayout are named and bracket the four text ids, which confirms the show-popup-text-then-close-window reading.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_HandleConfirmA
summary: Alternative confirm handler: when the window is active and the pad has a confirm event it resolves the target under the cursor and starts the action, otherwise returns 0.
evidence: No named callee besides the SE/popup helpers, and its guards (+0x405, f_4C & 0x102) are the same as 0x27FA20's, so it may be the same handler variant for another command page.

name: maybe_Ui_PartyPanel_CloseAllWindows
summary: Cancel/commit path of the battle party panel: clears the message args, hides the panel through its vtable, closes every window in the battle window list and asks the state controller for state 9.
evidence: Reached only from the handler table 0x728D9C and the window-list walk at +0x4260 is shared with 0x16B810; 'party panel' is not provable from the body alone.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_ShowSingleText
summary: Opens the message window on one fixed text: clears the list pane at +0x204, adds id 0x8B8 or 0x8B9 depending on a global flag bit, requests window state 0x11 and finishes the pane setup.
evidence: Ui_MessageWindow_ProcessCommands and Ui_MessageWindow_ReleaseLayout are its named callees and the state-0x11 request through vtable+0x4C ties it to the message window registered as 'win_message'; it is also listed among the battle popup window entries in Ui_BattlePopup_Show (0x27C2F0), which uses the same +0x204 pane.

name: Battle_PopupEntry_Create
signature: void* Battle_PopupEntry_Create(int self, unsigned short id, unsigned char kind, unsigned int arg4, unsigned char arg5, unsigned char arg6, unsigned int* extra)
summary: Creates a 0x24-byte battle popup entry (id, kind, flags, extra value) and inserts it into the popup lists, with an early-out for invalid targets.
evidence: Seven named callers (Ui_BattlePopup_Show, maybe_Battle_Ui_MemberWidget_PushPopup, maybe_Battle_UpdateUnitDisplay, Text_Scroll_UpdateStateMachine, ...) create popups through it, and the body fills +0x10/+0x12/+0x1A - confirmed as the popup-entry factory.

name: maybe_Ui_PartyPanel_ToggleAutoFlag
summary: Toggles the auto-battle/skip flag at GameWork+0x2D384 bit 0 when the panel is confirmed with a valid selection, then hides the panel and enters state 0xD.
evidence: Game_GetWork and Ui_BattlePopup_Show are named, but the same 0x2D384 bit0 test appears in the message-window opener (0x281150), so 'auto flag' is plausible yet unproven.

name: maybe_Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor
summary: Constructor of a small UI widget that owns a 12-entry list of 0x50-byte animation-reference records: installs vtable 0x0075DC34 after Ui_Object_CtorBase and default-constructs the twelve records at +0x4C.
evidence: Call sites are sub-object creations (Ui_ShopWindow_CreateSubObjects, Ui_ItemMenu_RootPart_Ctor, Ui_EquipmentRow_CtorSmall, Ui_PartySelectRowWidget_Ctor), and the body is just base ctor + vtable + std_ConstructArray of 12 x 0x50 records. The record size/content is inferred as animation refs, so the old AnimWidget12 name was replaced by the structure it actually owns.

name: maybe_Ui_DataPanel_OpenWithFlags
signature: void maybe_Ui_DataPanel_OpenWithFlags(DataPanel* self, u32 mode, char* flags)
summary: Opens the data/save panel with an option flag word: copies the 31 record strings, stamps the time hash and binds the labels before switching to the open state.
evidence: Recovered entry point with a damaged body; its neighbours Ui_Window_SetRowParamsAndRefresh and Save_SaveTask_StartSlot point at the save/data panel but not at a specific 'flags' variant.

name: maybe_Ui_DataPanel_OpenWithStrings
signature: void maybe_Ui_DataPanel_OpenWithStrings(DataPanel* self, u32 mode, char* flags)
summary: Opens the panel with its 31 text strings: copies 0x200 bytes per string into the buffer block, stamps the time hash, binds the two label panes and switches to state 5.
evidence: Callees Game_GetWork/Os_CalcTimeBasedHash/Save_InitPartySnapshot are named and the 31x0x200 copy loop is clear, but the panel's identity (save vs. data viewer) is unproven.

name: Svc_Time_GetCurrentTimestamp
summary: Returns the current 64-bit timestamp: the raw clock from maybe_Svc_ComputeClockMs multiplied by 1,000,000 plus the global epoch base g_007AEA28, written as a two-word value.
evidence: Correction: it belongs to the Svc_Time_* family (0x50ECxx-0x50Fxxx: ComposeTimestamp/GetTimestamp/IsValidDate) and the old name claimed milliseconds although the x1,000,000 scaling of the clock makes the unit unproven; its callers (Os_CalcTimeBasedHash, Field_InitSceneObjects, the icon cache) only need a monotonic stamp.

name: Field_Clock_GetDayOfMonth
summary: Returns the day of month of a timestamp: divides by one day and asks the calendar helper 0x0050EB54 for the third output field.
evidence: The three siblings are now called together from Os_CalcTimeBasedHash (0x2CDC44), which fixes the trio as the year/month/day split of one conversion.

name: Field_Clock_GetYear
summary: Returns the year of a timestamp through the first output field of the calendar helper 0x0050EB54.
evidence: Same divisor/offset as 0x658F0C and both are called from Os_CalcTimeBasedHash (0x2CDC44), so the year/month/day split is consistent.

name: Field_Clock_GetMonth
summary: Returns the month of a timestamp through the second output field of the calendar helper 0x0050EB54.
evidence: Companion of 0x658F0C/0x658FCC, all three called from Os_CalcTimeBasedHash; only the out-pointer position differs.

name: maybe_Ui_BigGridCursor_HandleInput
summary: Close/teardown path of a big grid widget: releases pack handles and layout refs, pops the dive-form pane and destroys the UI object.
evidence: Recovered entry point; the named neighbours Pack_ReleaseHandle, Pack_FreeHandleEntry, Ui_LayoutRef_Release and Ui_DiveForm_PopPane describe a teardown rather than input handling, so the old name may be wrong - kept as maybe_.

name: Gfx_Overlay_DrawSpriteTransition
signature: void Gfx_Overlay_DrawSpriteTransition(void* gfx, void* cmd, unsigned int ctx, void* set, void* sprite, void* bank, unsigned int* texState, float* fromPos, unsigned int extraColor, unsigned int extraAlpha, float* toPos)
summary: Transition variant of the overlay sprite draw: interpolates position and colour by the s0 factor, optionally emits the extra tinted bar quad (command 0x80000008) and writes the normal or extra texture command block.
evidence: Its caller Gfx_Overlay_DrawSpriteListTransition (0x5779C8) and the named callees Gfx_GpuCmd_WriteTextureUnitBlock, Gfx_CmdBuf_WriteDepthStencilRegisters and Gfx_Pica_EmitModelTextureBindings confirm the sprite-draw path.

name: maybe_Gfx_SortAndSubmitByPriority
signature: void maybe_Gfx_SortAndSubmitByPriority(RenderElement* self, unsigned int pass, void** list, unsigned int arg4, unsigned int arg5)
summary: Collects a doubly-linked list, orders the elements by their key byte +0x22 and submits each through Gfx_Overlay_DrawSpriteListTransition with the element's +0x88 value as key.
evidence: The only named callee is Gfx_Overlay_DrawSpriteListTransition, used from the main-screen overlay draws (0x2D36C8/0x2D3E1A); 'by priority' is inferred from the +0x22 comparison.

name: maybe_Ui_AnimClip_CtorFromData
signature: UiAnimClip* maybe_Ui_AnimClip_CtorFromData(UiAnimClip* self, int arg2, float* data)
summary: Constructs a UI animation clip from a serialised track table: installs vtable 0x781348, sets up the intrusive list and copies the keyframe times/values before the shared runtime init.
evidence: Six named Ui_Layout* ctors (Pane/Parts/Picture/TextBox/Window/CreatePaneByFourCC) call it, which confirms it as the animation member of every layout element; the vtable's mix of clip and widget methods keeps the class name uncertain.

name: maybe_Ui_AnimClip_CtorEmpty
summary: Constructs an empty UI animation clip (vtable 0x781348, zeroed tracks, no loop) and runs the shared runtime initialiser.
evidence: Same vtable/list setup as 0x5387EC, called from Ui_LayoutPicture_InitAnimation (0x53ECF0) and Ui_AnimClip_ResetDefault (0x6EF69C); the clip-vs-widget ambiguity of vtable 0x781348 remains.

name: maybe_Ui_AnimClip_CtorCopy
summary: Copy-constructs a UI animation clip: same vtable 0x781348, copies the duration/loop fields (f_1C..f_24) from the descriptor and initialises the keyframe buffer.
evidence: Called from Ui_LayoutPane_BindChildren (0x53ED98) and copies f_1C/f_20/f_24 like 0x5387EC; class name still uncertain for the same vtable reason.

name: maybe_Ui_AnimClip_InitRuntime
summary: Common runtime initialiser of the UI animation clip: clears the track count/first/last pointers, runs the one-time global init guard and initialises the 0x48-byte keyframe buffer.
evidence: Called from both clip constructors (0x5387EC, 0x538C04), so the runtime role is solid, but the owning class is only known as 'the layout element animation member'.

name: Font_GlyphQuad_CreateFromUVs
signature: GlyphQuad* Font_GlyphQuad_CreateFromUVs(GlyphQuad* storage, FontContext* ctx, u32 texId, int arg4, u32 arg5, u32 arg6, int* uv0, int* uv1, int* uv2, int* uv3)
summary: Creates a textured glyph/sprite quad: initialises the base object, copies the four UV corner triples, sets the font scale from the context mode, converts the UV rectangle into an atlas cell index and links it into the quad list.
evidence: Callees Font_GlyphQuad_SetUV/SetUVTriple and Field2D_SpriteNode_Draw place it next to the glyph-quad creation path, and the 0xAAAAAAAB divide-by-3/cell arithmetic plus table 0x727BF0 fixes the atlas-cell step.

name: maybe_Text_SpanCursor_Init
signature: SpanCursor* maybe_Text_SpanCursor_Init(SpanCursor* self, TextContext* ctx, int mode)
summary: Initialises a span cursor sub-object: installs vtable 0x783BA0, stores the context, computes the first index from the context's f_78 with 0x6685EC and clears the direction/flag/count fields.
evidence: The only caller is Field2D_SpriteNode_UpdateAnimation (0x5CA54C) with (&self->f_a8, self+8), i.e. a sprite node, not a text window, so the 'text span cursor' reading is not supported by the caller; the vtable/ctx store itself is clear.

name: maybe_Field2D_Map_RebuildOverlayC
summary: Map overlay refresh: clears through Field2D_SpriteNode_UpdateAnimation, releases the current object, rebuilds it with 0x005CC878 and reinstalls it.
evidence: No caller and the only named callee is Field2D_SpriteNode_UpdateAnimation; the 'map overlay' scope comes from the 0x67xxxx map block, so the exact object stays open.

name: Gfx_GetRenderContext
summary: Lazily creates and returns the process-wide 0x1F8-byte render/graphics context singleton (guard g_001053B4, instance g_001053B8).
evidence: 28 callers, all in the battle UI flow and the gfx passes (Battle_UiFlow_Open*Window, 0x5668A0-0x56AFFC, 0x616DB4), plus the same 0x100050-ctor shape used by the other lazy singletons - confirmed as the shared context getter.

name: Engine_DispatchFrameCallbacks
summary: Frame callback dispatcher: runs up to four registered {fn,arg} callbacks from each of the global frame-begin/render/frame-end arrays, between the semaphore lock/unlock and the runtime-state guards.
evidence: Os_LockSemaphore, Os_ReentrantLock_Acquire and Os_TryLockSemaphore are named now, and it is called from both Engine_Initialize (0x101B74) and the main loop (0x694E18) - the per-frame callback pump is confirmed.

name: maybe_Snd_StreamManager_Update
summary: Per-frame update of the streamed-audio manager: advances the five fade records, updates all stream slots and voices, then flushes the texture uploads it owns and releases the finished ones.
evidence: Correction: the named callees are Snd_StreamSlot_UpdateAll (0x105584, the six streamed-audio slot banks) and Snd_StreamVoice_Update (0x105AFC), so this is the audio-stream frame update, not a gfx task pump; only the trailing Gfx_UploadQueuedTextures/ReleaseFinishedUploads calls made the old 'Gfx' name plausible.

name: maybe_Engine_SubmitFrameEntries
summary: Frame submission step: runs maybe_Snd_UpdateVoiceList, then invokes every queued entry vtable+0x20 with the fixed arguments (0x3F, a stack buffer, 0x100, 10). Called from Engine_Initialize and the main loop.
evidence: The only named callees are Pack_HandleTable_Get and maybe_Snd_UpdateVoiceList; the queued objects and the 0x20 slot are not identified, and the sound call makes the old Gfx_SubmitDrawList name an unsupported guess. Kept as a generic frame-submission step at 0.4.

name: maybe_Gfx_ReleaseRenderContext
summary: Flushes the renderer and destroys the owned renderer object (vtable+4), clearing the pointer.
evidence: Pack_HandleTable_Get is named and the teardown is called from the main-loop shutdown path 0x694E18 symmetric with 0x10411C; the object at f_18 is not otherwise identified.

name: maybe_Fs_Channel_InitFields
signature: u32 maybe_Fs_Channel_InitFields(FsChannel* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Initialises one transfer channel: stores its heap/callback pointer, builds the list head at +0xE104/+0xE118 and creates the asynchronous transfer primitive with the 0x2000-byte staging buffer.
evidence: Gfx_CommandBuffer_Submit is named but the channel itself is only described by the +0xE1xx fields; called once from Engine_Initialize (0x101B74) with the cache-set base.
